raw: Act 2, Scene 2 — Capulet’s Garden

sentences.en: Capulet’s Garden
sentences.ko: 캐퓰릿 집의 정원

summary.en: At her window, Juliet speaks of her love, and Romeo hears her. They promise to marry.
summary.ko: 줄리엣이 창가에서 사랑을 고백하고, 로미오가 그 말을 듣는다. 두 사람은 결혼을 약속한다.

raw: Enter Romeo.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: He jests at scars that never felt a wound.

sentences.en: Someone who never felt a wound jokes about scars.
sentences.ko: 상처를 입어본 적 없는 사람이 흉터에 대해 농담을 한다.

raw: Juliet appears above at a window.

sentences.en: Juliet appears at a window above.
sentences.ko: 줄리엣이 위쪽 창가에 나타난다.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
But soft, what light through yonder window breaks?
It is the east, and Juliet is the sun!
Arise fair sun and kill the envious moon,
Who is already sick and pale with grief,
That thou her maid art far more fair than she.
Be not her maid since she is envious;
Her vestal livery is but sick and green,
And none but fools do wear it; cast it off.
It is my lady, O it is my love!
O, that she knew she were!
She speaks, yet she says nothing. What of that?
Her eye discourses, I will answer it.
I am too bold, ’tis not to me she speaks.
Two of the fairest stars in all the heaven,
Having some business, do entreat her eyes
To twinkle in their spheres till they return.
What if her eyes were there, they in her head?
The brightness of her cheek would shame those stars,
As daylight doth a lamp; her eyes in heaven
Would through the airy region stream so bright
That birds would sing and think it were not night.
See how she leans her cheek upon her hand.
O that I were a glove upon that hand,
That I might touch that cheek.

sentences.en: Wait, what light breaks through that window over there?
sentences.ko: 잠깐, 저기 창문 너머로 비치는 빛은 무엇인가?

sentences.en: It is the east, and Juliet is the sun!
sentences.ko: 저건 동쪽이고, 줄리엣은 태양이다!

sentences.en: Rise, fair sun, and kill the envious moon.
sentences.ko: 아름다운 태양이여, 떠올라 질투에 찬 달을 없애라.

sentences.en: The moon is already sick and pale with grief.
sentences.ko: 달은 이미 슬픔으로 병들고 창백해졌다.

sentences.en: She is jealous because you, her servant, are far more beautiful than she is.
sentences.ko: 달은 자기 시녀인 네가 자기보다 훨씬 아름다워서 질투한다.

sentences.en: Do not be her servant since she is jealous.
sentences.ko: 달이 질투하니 달의 시녀가 되지 마라.

sentences.en: Her uniform of virginity is only sick and green.
sentences.ko: 달이 주는 순결의 옷은 병든 초록빛일 뿐이다.

sentences.en: Only fools wear it; throw it off.
sentences.ko: 바보들만이 그것을 입으니, 벗어버려라.

sentences.en: It is my lady. Oh, it is my love!
sentences.ko: 저건 나의 여인이다. 오, 나의 사랑이다!

sentences.en: Oh, if only she knew she was my love!
sentences.ko: 오, 그녀가 자신이 내 사랑임을 알기만 한다면!

sentences.en: She speaks, yet she says nothing. What of that?
sentences.ko: 그녀가 말을 한다. 그러나 아무 말도 없다. 그게 어떻단 말인가?

sentences.en: Her eyes communicate, and I will answer them.
sentences.ko: 그녀의 눈이 말을 건네고, 나는 그에 답할 것이다.

sentences.en: I am too bold. She is not speaking to me.
sentences.ko: 내가 너무 대담하다. 그녀는 나에게 말하는 것이 아니다.

sentences.en: Two of the most beautiful stars in all heaven have some business.
sentences.ko: 하늘에서 가장 아름다운 별 두 개가 볼일이 있어 자리를 비운다.

sentences.en: They ask her eyes to shine in their places until they return.
sentences.ko: 그들이 돌아올 때까지 대신 빛나달라고 그녀의 눈에 부탁했다.

sentences.en: What if her eyes were there and those stars were in her head?
sentences.ko: 만약 그녀의 눈이 그 자리에 있고 저 별들이 그녀의 머릿속에 있다면 어떨까?

sentences.en: The brightness of her cheek would shame those stars, just as daylight shames a lamp.
sentences.ko: 그녀의 뺨은 낮의 빛이 등불을 무색하게 하듯 저 별들을 부끄럽게 할 것이다.

sentences.en: Her eyes in heaven would shine so brightly through the air.
sentences.ko: 하늘에 있는 그녀의 눈은 공중에서 아주 밝게 빛날 것이다.

sentences.en: Birds would sing and think it was not night.
sentences.ko: 새들은 노래하며 밤이 아니라고 생각할 것이다.

sentences.en: See how she leans her cheek on her hand.
sentences.ko: 그녀가 손에 뺨을 기대고 있는 것을 보라.

sentences.en: Oh, I wish I were a glove on that hand.
sentences.ko: 오, 내가 저 손에 끼워진 장갑이라면 좋겠다.

sentences.en: Then I could touch that cheek.
sentences.ko: 그러면 저 뺨을 만질 수 있을 텐데.

speaker: JULIET
raw: Ay me.

sentences.en: Oh, dear me.
sentences.ko: 아, 슬프구나.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
She speaks.
O speak again bright angel, for thou art
As glorious to this night, being o’er my head,
As is a winged messenger of heaven
Unto the white-upturned wondering eyes
Of mortals that fall back to gaze on him
When he bestrides the lazy-puffing clouds
And sails upon the bosom of the air.

sentences.en: She speaks.
sentences.ko: 그녀가 말해요.

sentences.en: Oh, speak again, bright angel.
sentences.ko: 오, 다시 말해줘요, 빛나는 천사여.

sentences.en: Up above my head tonight, you shine like an angel from heaven.
sentences.ko: 오늘 밤 내 머리 위에서 당신은 하늘에서 온 천사처럼 빛나요.

sentences.en: People fall back and stare up at such an angel with wide, wondering eyes.
sentences.ko: 사람들은 뒤로 물러나서 그런 천사를 놀라운 눈으로 바라봐요.

sentences.en: He rides on the lazy, drifting clouds.
sentences.ko: 천사는 느릿하게 떠가는 구름을 타고 가요.

sentences.en: He sails through the air.
sentences.ko: 공중을 가르며 항해하지요.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
O Romeo, Romeo, wherefore art thou Romeo?
Deny thy father and refuse thy name.
Or if thou wilt not, be but sworn my love,
And I’ll no longer be a Capulet.

sentences.en: Oh Romeo, Romeo, why are you Romeo?
sentences.ko: 오 로미오, 로미오, 왜 당신은 로미오인가요?

sentences.en: Deny your father and refuse your name.
sentences.ko: 아버지를 버리고 당신의 이름을 버리세요.

sentences.en: Or if you will not, just swear that you love me.
sentences.ko: 그게 안 된다면, 그저 나를 사랑한다고 맹세하세요.

sentences.en: Then I will no longer be a Capulet.
sentences.ko: 그러면 난 더 이상 캐퓰릿이 아니에요.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: Shall I hear more, or shall I speak at this?

sentences.en: Shall I hear more, or shall I speak now?
sentences.ko: 더 들어야 할까, 아니면 이제 내가 말해야 할까?

speaker: JULIET
raw:
’Tis but thy name that is my enemy;
Thou art thyself, though not a Montague.
What’s Montague? It is nor hand nor foot,
Nor arm, nor face, nor any other part
Belonging to a man. O be some other name.
What’s in a name? That which we call a rose
By any other name would smell as sweet;
So Romeo would, were he not Romeo call’d,
Retain that dear perfection which he owes
Without that title. Romeo, doff thy name,
And for thy name, which is no part of thee,
Take all myself.

sentences.en: It is only your name that is my enemy.
sentences.ko: 내 적은 당신의 이름뿐이에요.

sentences.en: You are yourself, even if you are not a Montague.
sentences.ko: 당신이 몬태규가 아니더라도 당신은 당신일 뿐이에요.

sentences.en: What is a Montague? It is not a hand or a foot.
sentences.ko: 몬태규가 무엇인가요? 손이나 발 같은 게 아니에요.

sentences.en: It is not an arm, a face, or any other part of a man.
sentences.ko: 팔이나 얼굴, 혹은 사람의 다른 신체 부위도 아니고요.

sentences.en: Oh, take some other name.
sentences.ko: 오, 다른 이름을 가지세요.

sentences.en: What is in a name?
sentences.ko: 이름에 무슨 의미가 있겠어요?

sentences.en: A rose would smell as sweet if we called it by another name.
sentences.ko: 장미를 다른 이름으로 불러도 향기는 여전히 달콤할 거예요.

sentences.en: So Romeo would keep his perfection if he were not called Romeo.
sentences.ko: 로미오라는 이름이 아니었다면 로미오는 여전히 완벽했을 거예요.

sentences.en: He would have that quality without the title.
sentences.ko: 그 호칭이 없어도 그 고귀함은 그대로였을 거예요.

sentences.en: Romeo, throw off your name.
sentences.ko: 로미오, 당신의 이름을 버리세요.

sentences.en: Instead of your name, which is no part of you, take all of me.
sentences.ko: 당신의 일부도 아닌 그 이름 대신, 나의 전부를 받아주세요.

speaker: ROMEO

sentences.en: I accept your promise.
sentences.ko: 당신의 약속을 받아들일게요.

sentences.en: Just call me love, and I will be baptized again.
sentences.ko: 그저 나를 '사랑'이라고 불러 주세요, 그러면 새로 세례를 받을게요.

sentences.en: From now on, I will never be Romeo.
sentences.ko: 이제부터 나는 결코 로미오가 아니에요.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
What man art thou that, thus bescreen’d in night
So stumblest on my counsel?

sentences.en: What man are you?
sentences.ko: 당신은 어떤 분이신가요?

sentences.en: You are hidden in the night.
sentences.ko: 밤의 어둠 속에 숨어 계시네요.

sentences.en: How did you happen to overhear my private thoughts?
sentences.ko: 어떻게 제 은밀한 생각을 엿들으신 거죠?

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
By a name
I know not how to tell thee who I am:
My name, dear saint, is hateful to myself,
Because it is an enemy to thee.
Had I it written, I would tear the word.

sentences.en: I do not know how to tell you who I am because of a name.
sentences.ko: 이름 때문에 내가 누구인지 말하기 어렵네요.

sentences.en: My name, dear saint, is hateful to me.
sentences.ko: 사랑스러운 성녀여, 내 이름은 나도 싫어요.

sentences.en: It is because it is an enemy to you.
sentences.ko: 그건 당신에게 적대적인 이름이기 때문이죠.

sentences.en: If I had it written down, I would tear the word away.
sentences.ko: 만약 이 이름이 적혀 있다면, 나는 그 글자를 찢어버릴 거예요.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
My ears have yet not drunk a hundred words
Of thy tongue’s utterance, yet I know the sound.
Art thou not Romeo, and a Montague?

sentences.en: I have not heard a hundred words from your mouth yet.
sentences.ko: 당신의 입에서 나온 말을 백 마디도 듣지 못했어요.

sentences.en: Still, I know the sound of your voice.
sentences.ko: 그럼에도 당신의 목소리는 알 수 있어요.

sentences.en: Are you not Romeo and a Montague?
sentences.ko: 당신은 로미오이자 몬태규가 아닌가요?

speaker: ROMEO
raw: Neither, fair maid, if either thee dislike.

sentences.en: I am neither, beautiful girl, if you dislike either of those things.
sentences.ko: 아름다운 아가씨, 당신이 싫다면 나는 그 어느 쪽도 아니에요.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
How cam’st thou hither, tell me, and wherefore?
The orchard walls are high and hard to climb,
And the place death, considering who thou art,
If any of my kinsmen find thee here.

sentences.en: Tell me how you came here and why.
sentences.ko: 어떻게, 왜 여기까지 왔는지 말해줘요.

sentences.en: The orchard walls are high and hard to climb.
sentences.ko: 과수원 담은 높아서 넘기 힘들어요.

sentences.en: Because of who you are, this place means death if any of my relatives find you here.
sentences.ko: 당신이 누구인지 알기에, 내 친척들이 당신을 발견하면 이곳은 죽음의 장소가 될 거예요.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
With love’s light wings did I o’erperch these walls,
For stony limits cannot hold love out,
And what love can do, that dares love attempt:
Therefore thy kinsmen are no stop to me.

sentences.en: I flew over these walls on love's light wings.
sentences.ko: 나는 사랑의 가벼운 날개를 타고 이 담을 넘어왔어요.

sentences.en: Stone walls cannot keep love out.
sentences.ko: 돌담은 사랑을 막아낼 수 없어요.

sentences.en: Whatever love can do, love dares to try.
sentences.ko: 사랑이 할 수 있는 일이라면, 사랑은 무엇이든 시도하니까요.

sentences.en: Therefore, your relatives are no stop to me.
sentences.ko: 그러니 당신의 친척들도 나를 막을 수 없어요.

speaker: JULIET
raw: If they do see thee, they will murder thee.

sentences.en: If they see you, they will murder you.
sentences.ko: 그들이 당신을 본다면 죽일 거예요.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Alack, there lies more peril in thine eye
Than twenty of their swords. Look thou but sweet,
And I am proof against their enmity.

sentences.en: Oh no, there is more danger in your eyes than in twenty of their swords.
sentences.ko: 아, 당신의 눈 속에는 그들의 칼 스무 자루보다 더 큰 위험이 있어요.

sentences.en: Just look sweet, and I will be protected from their hatred.
sentences.ko: 그저 아름답게만 보여주세요, 그러면 그들의 증오로부터 보호받을 수 있을 거예요.

speaker: JULIET
raw: I would not for the world they saw thee here.

sentences.en: I would not let them see you here for anything.
sentences.ko: 어떤 일이 있어도 당신이 여기서 들키는 걸 허락할 수 없어요.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
I have night’s cloak to hide me from their eyes,
And but thou love me, let them find me here.
My life were better ended by their hate
Than death prorogued, wanting of thy love.

sentences.en: I have the night's cloak to hide me from their eyes.
sentences.ko: 밤의 망토가 그들의 눈으로부터 나를 숨겨 줄 거예요.

sentences.en: And if you love me, let them find me here.
sentences.ko: 나를 사랑한다면, 그들이 여기서 나를 찾게 내버려 두세요.

sentences.en: My life would be better ended by their hate than delayed without your love.
sentences.ko: 당신의 사랑 없이 목숨을 이어가느니 그들의 증오에 죽는 게 나아요.

speaker: JULIET
raw: By whose direction found’st thou out this place?

sentences.en: Who told you how to find this place?
sentences.ko: 어떻게 이곳을 찾아오는지 누가 알려줬나요?

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
By love, that first did prompt me to enquire;
He lent me counsel, and I lent him eyes.
I am no pilot; yet wert thou as far
As that vast shore wash’d with the farthest sea,
I should adventure for such merchandise.

sentences.en: Love first prompted me to ask.
sentences.ko: 사랑이 먼저 나를 부추겨 묻게 했어요.

sentences.en: It gave me advice, and I gave it eyes.
sentences.ko: 사랑이 내게 조언을 했고, 나는 사랑에게 내 눈을 빌려줬죠.

sentences.en: I am not a pilot.
sentences.ko: 저는 항해사가 아니에요.

sentences.en: You could be as far away as the shore of the most distant sea.
sentences.ko: 당신은 아주 먼 바다의 해안선만큼 멀리 있을 수도 있죠.

sentences.en: Even then, I would take the risk for such a prize.
sentences.ko: 그래도 나는 그런 보물을 위해 기꺼이 위험을 무릅쓸 거예요.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Thou knowest the mask of night is on my face,
Else would a maiden blush bepaint my cheek
For that which thou hast heard me speak tonight.
Fain would I dwell on form, fain, fain deny
What I have spoke; but farewell compliment.
Dost thou love me? I know thou wilt say Ay,
And I will take thy word. Yet, if thou swear’st,
Thou mayst prove false. At lovers’ perjuries,
They say Jove laughs. O gentle Romeo,
If thou dost love, pronounce it faithfully.
Or if thou thinkest I am too quickly won,
I’ll frown and be perverse, and say thee nay,
So thou wilt woo. But else, not for the world.
In truth, fair Montague, I am too fond;
And therefore thou mayst think my ’haviour light:
But trust me, gentleman, I’ll prove more true
Than those that have more cunning to be strange.
I should have been more strange, I must confess,
But that thou overheard’st, ere I was ’ware,
My true-love passion; therefore pardon me,
And not impute this yielding to light love,
Which the dark night hath so discovered.

sentences.en: You know the mask of night is on my face.
sentences.ko: 밤이라는 가면을 쓰고 있다는 걸 아시잖아요.

sentences.en: Otherwise, a girl's blush would color my cheek for what you heard me say tonight.
sentences.ko: 그러지 않았다면, 오늘 밤 제가 한 말 때문에 소녀의 얼굴이 부끄러움으로 붉어졌을 거예요.

sentences.en: I would gladly act properly and politely.
sentences.ko: 기꺼이 예의 바르고 정중하게 행동했을 거예요.

sentences.en: I would gladly, gladly deny what I said.
sentences.ko: 제가 한 말을 기꺼이, 기꺼이 부정했을 거예요.

sentences.en: But I give up polite behavior.
sentences.ko: 하지만 이제 예의 차리는 건 포기할게요.

sentences.en: Do you love me?
sentences.ko: 저를 사랑하시나요?

sentences.en: I know you will say yes, and I will take your word.
sentences.ko: 당신이 그렇다고 말할 걸 알고 있고, 저는 그 말을 믿을 거예요.

sentences.en: Yet, if you swear it, you might prove false.
sentences.ko: 하지만 당신이 맹세한다 해도 거짓일 수 있어요.

sentences.en: They say Jove laughs at lovers' broken promises.
sentences.ko: 사람들은 주피터 신이 연인들의 거짓 맹세를 비웃는다고 해요.

sentences.en: Oh gentle Romeo, if you love me, say it faithfully.
sentences.ko: 오, 다정한 로미오, 나를 사랑한다면 진심으로 말해 줘요.

sentences.en: Or if you think I am too easily won, I will frown and be stubborn.
sentences.ko: 혹시 제가 너무 쉽게 얻어지는 존재라고 생각하신다면, 제가 찡그리며 고집을 피울게요.

sentences.en: I will say no, so that you will try to win my love.
sentences.ko: 당신이 제 사랑을 얻으려 노력하게 하려고 '아니오'라고 말할 거예요.

sentences.en: But otherwise, not for the world.
sentences.ko: 하지만 그렇지 않다면, 절대로 안 돼요.

sentences.en: In truth, fair Montague, I love you too much.
sentences.ko: 사실, 아름다운 몬태규, 저는 당신을 너무나 사랑해요.

sentences.en: Therefore you might think my behavior is not serious.
sentences.ko: 그래서 제 행동이 진지하지 않다고 생각하실 수도 있어요.

sentences.en: But trust me, gentleman, I will prove more true than other girls.
sentences.ko: 하지만 믿어주세요, 신사분, 저는 다른 소녀들보다 더 진실함을 증명할 거예요.

sentences.en: They are only better at pretending not to care.
sentences.ko: 그들은 단지 상관없는 척하는 데 더 능숙할 뿐이에요.

sentences.en: I should have been more distant, I must confess.
sentences.ko: 솔직히 말하면, 제가 좀 더 거리를 뒀어야 했다고 고백해요.

sentences.en: But you overheard my true love passion before I was aware.
sentences.ko: 하지만 제가 알아차리기 전에 당신은 제 진실한 사랑의 열정을 들었죠.

sentences.en: Therefore forgive me.
sentences.ko: 그러니 저를 용서해 주세요.

sentences.en: Do not blame my quick yes on a light love; the dark night revealed it.
sentences.ko: 제 빠른 대답을 가벼운 사랑 때문이라고 탓하지 마세요. 어두운 밤이 그것을 드러낸 것이니까요.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Lady, by yonder blessed moon I vow,
That tips with silver all these fruit-tree tops,—

sentences.en: Lady, by that blessed moon over there I vow, that tips all these fruit-tree tops with silver—
sentences.ko: 아가씨, 저기 과일나무 꼭대기를 은빛으로 물들이는 축복받은 달을 걸고 맹세해요—

speaker: JULIET
raw:
O swear not by the moon, th’inconstant moon,
That monthly changes in her circled orb,
Lest that thy love prove likewise variable.

sentences.en: Oh, do not swear by the moon.
sentences.ko: 오, 달을 두고 맹세하지 마세요.

sentences.en: The moon is always changing.
sentences.ko: 달은 항상 변하니까요.

sentences.en: It changes every month in its circle.
sentences.ko: 그것은 매달 그 궤도 안에서 변해요.

sentences.en: I do not want your love to change like that.
sentences.ko: 당신의 사랑이 그렇게 변하는 걸 원치 않아요.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: What shall I swear by?

sentences.en: What should I swear by?
sentences.ko: 그럼 무엇으로 맹세하면 될까요?

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Do not swear at all.
Or if thou wilt, swear by thy gracious self,
Which is the god of my idolatry,
And I’ll believe thee.

sentences.en: Do not swear at all.
sentences.ko: 아무것도 맹세하지 마세요.

sentences.en: Or if you want to, swear by your gracious self.
sentences.ko: 정 맹세하고 싶다면 당신 자신을 걸고 맹세하세요.

sentences.en: You are the god of my worship.
sentences.ko: 당신은 제가 숭배하는 신과 같은 분이니까요.

sentences.en: Then I will believe you.
sentences.ko: 그럼 당신의 말을 믿을게요.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: If my heart’s dear love,—

sentences.en: If my heart's dear love—
sentences.ko: 내 마음속 소중한 사랑이—

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Well, do not swear. Although I joy in thee,
I have no joy of this contract tonight;
It is too rash, too unadvis’d, too sudden,
Too like the lightning, which doth cease to be
Ere one can say “It lightens.” Sweet, good night.
This bud of love, by summer’s ripening breath,
May prove a beauteous flower when next we meet.
Good night, good night. As sweet repose and rest
Come to thy heart as that within my breast.

sentences.en: Well, do not swear.
sentences.ko: 음, 맹세하지 마세요.

sentences.en: Although I find joy in you, I have no joy in this contract tonight.
sentences.ko: 당신을 통해 기쁨을 느끼지만, 오늘 밤의 이 약속은 기쁘지 않아요.

sentences.en: It is too rash, not thought through, and too sudden.
sentences.ko: 너무 성급하고 깊이 생각하지 않았으며 너무 갑작스럽거든요.

sentences.en: It is like lightning, which stops before one can say 'It lightens'.
sentences.ko: 마치 '번쩍'이라고 말하기도 전에 멈춰버리는 번개와 같아요.

sentences.en: Good night.
sentences.ko: 안녕히 주무세요.

sentences.en: With summer's warm breath, this bud of love may be a beautiful flower when we next meet.
sentences.ko: 여름의 따스한 숨결 속에서, 이 사랑의 싹은 우리가 다음에 만날 때 아름다운 꽃이 될 거예요.

sentences.en: Good night, good night.
sentences.ko: 잘 자요, 잘 자요.

sentences.en: May the same sweet peace that is in my heart come to your heart.
sentences.ko: 내 마음속에 있는 달콤한 평화가 당신의 마음에도 깃들기를 바라요.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: O wilt thou leave me so unsatisfied?

sentences.en: Oh, will you leave me so unsatisfied?
sentences.ko: 오, 저를 이렇게 허전하게 두고 가실 건가요?

speaker: JULIET
raw: What satisfaction canst thou have tonight?

sentences.en: What satisfaction can you have tonight?
sentences.ko: 오늘 밤 당신이 어떤 만족을 얻을 수 있겠어요?

speaker: ROMEO
raw: Th’exchange of thy love’s faithful vow for mine.

sentences.en: The exchange of your faithful vow for mine.
sentences.ko: 당신의 진실한 맹세와 내 맹세를 바꾸는 것이요.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
I gave thee mine before thou didst request it;
And yet I would it were to give again.

sentences.en: I gave you mine before you asked for it.
sentences.ko: 당신이 요청하기도 전에 저는 이미 제 것을 드렸어요.

sentences.en: And yet I wish I could give it again.
sentences.ko: 그런데도 다시 한번 드릴 수 있다면 좋겠어요.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: Would’st thou withdraw it? For what purpose, love?

sentences.en: Would you take it back?
sentences.ko: 그 맹세를 거두어 가겠다는 건가요?

sentences.en: For what reason, my love?
sentences.ko: 어떤 이유 때문인가요, 내 사랑?

speaker: JULIET
raw:
But to be frank and give it thee again.
And yet I wish but for the thing I have;
My bounty is as boundless as the sea,
My love as deep; the more I give to thee,
The more I have, for both are infinite.
I hear some noise within. Dear love, adieu.

sentences.en: I want to be generous and give it to you again.
sentences.ko: 관대하게 당신에게 다시 주고 싶어요.

sentences.en: Yet I only want the thing I already have.
sentences.ko: 하지만 저는 이미 가진 것을 원할 뿐이에요.

sentences.en: My generosity is as boundless as the sea, and my love is just as deep.
sentences.ko: 제 관대함은 바다처럼 끝이 없고, 제 사랑도 그만큼 깊답니다.

sentences.en: The more I give to you, the more I have because both are infinite.
sentences.ko: 두 가지 모두 무한하기에, 드릴수록 더 많이 갖게 되는 거예요.

sentences.en: I hear some noise from inside.
sentences.ko: 안에서 소리가 들려요.

sentences.en: My dear love, goodbye.
sentences.ko: 사랑하는 내 사람, 안녕히 가세요.

raw: Nurse calls within.

sentences.en: The Nurse calls from inside.
sentences.ko: 유모가 안에서 부른다.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Anon, good Nurse!—Sweet Montague be true.
Stay but a little, I will come again.

sentences.en: Coming, good Nurse!
sentences.ko: 금방 가요, 유모!

sentences.en: Sweet Montague, be true.
sentences.ko: 다정한 몬태규, 변하지 말아요.

sentences.en: Wait just a little, for I will come back again.
sentences.ko: 잠시만 기다려요, 제가 다시 돌아올게요.

raw: Exit.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
O blessed, blessed night. I am afeard,
Being in night, all this is but a dream,
Too flattering sweet to be substantial.

sentences.en: Oh, blessed, blessed night.
sentences.ko: 오, 축복받은 밤이구나.

sentences.en: I am afraid.
sentences.ko: 두렵다.

sentences.en: Since it is night, all of this might be a dream.
sentences.ko: 밤이니 이 모든 것이 꿈일지도 모른다.

sentences.en: It is too sweet to be real.
sentences.ko: 현실이라기엔 너무나 달콤하다.

raw: Enter Juliet above.

sentences.en: Juliet comes back to the window.
sentences.ko: 줄리엣이 창가로 돌아온다.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Three words, dear Romeo, and good night indeed.
If that thy bent of love be honourable,
Thy purpose marriage, send me word tomorrow,
By one that I’ll procure to come to thee,
Where and what time thou wilt perform the rite,
And all my fortunes at thy foot I’ll lay
And follow thee my lord throughout the world.

sentences.en: Three words, dear Romeo, and then really good night.
sentences.ko: 사랑하는 로미오, 세 마디만 말하고 이제 정말 자러 가겠어요.

sentences.en: If your love is honorable and your plan is marriage, send me word tomorrow.
sentences.ko: 당신의 사랑이 진실하고 결혼할 생각이라면 내일 소식을 전해줘요.

sentences.en: I will find someone to come to you.
sentences.ko: 당신에게 올 사람을 찾아낼게요.

sentences.en: Through that person, tell me where and at what time we will marry.
sentences.ko: 그 사람을 통해 어디서 언제 결혼할지 알려주세요.

sentences.en: I will give all my fortunes at your feet and follow you as my lord throughout the world.
sentences.ko: 내 모든 재산을 당신 발밑에 바치고 세상 어디든 당신을 주인으로 모시며 따를게요.

speaker: NURSE
raw: Madam.

sentences.en: Madam.
sentences.ko: 아가씨.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
I come, anon.— But if thou meanest not well,
I do beseech thee,—

sentences.en: I am coming right away.
sentences.ko: 지금 바로 갈게.

sentences.en: But if you do not mean well, I beg you—
sentences.ko: 하지만 나쁜 뜻이라면, 부탁하는데—

speaker: NURSE
raw: Madam.

sentences.en: Madam.
sentences.ko: 아가씨.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
By and by I come—
To cease thy strife and leave me to my grief.
Tomorrow will I send.

sentences.en: I will come in a moment.
sentences.ko: 금방 갈게.

sentences.en: Stop trying, and leave me to my sadness.
sentences.ko: 그만하고 내 슬픔을 그냥 내버려 둬.

sentences.en: I will send word tomorrow.
sentences.ko: 내일 소식을 전할게.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: So thrive my soul,—

sentences.en: As I hope for heaven—
sentences.ko: 천국을 걸고 맹세하건대—

speaker: JULIET
raw: A thousand times good night.

sentences.en: Good night a thousand times.
sentences.ko: 천 번이라도 잘 자요.

raw: Exit.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
A thousand times the worse, to want thy light.
Love goes toward love as schoolboys from their books,
But love from love, towards school with heavy looks.

sentences.en: It is a thousand times worse without your light.
sentences.ko: 당신의 빛이 없으니 천 배는 더 괴로워요.

sentences.en: Love goes toward love as happily as schoolboys leave their books.
sentences.ko: 사랑은 학생이 책을 두고 뛰쳐나가듯 기쁘게 사랑에게 가요.

sentences.en: But love leaves love as sadly as schoolboys go to school.
sentences.ko: 하지만 사랑은 학생이 학교에 가듯 풀이 죽어 사랑을 떠나요.

raw: Retiring slowly.

sentences.en: Romeo moves away slowly.
sentences.ko: 로미오가 천천히 멀어진다.

raw: Re-enter Juliet, above.

sentences.en: Juliet comes back to the window.
sentences.ko: 줄리엣이 다시 창가로 온다.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Hist! Romeo, hist! O for a falconer’s voice
To lure this tassel-gentle back again.
Bondage is hoarse and may not speak aloud,
Else would I tear the cave where Echo lies,
And make her airy tongue more hoarse than mine
With repetition of my Romeo’s name.

sentences.en: Psst! Romeo, psst!
sentences.ko: 쉿! 로미오, 쉿!

sentences.en: Oh, I wish for a falconer's voice.
sentences.ko: 아, 매사냥꾼의 목소리가 있으면 좋겠어요.

sentences.en: I want to call Romeo back, the way a falconer calls back his hawk.
sentences.ko: 매사냥꾼이 매를 부르듯 로미오를 불러들이고 싶어요.

sentences.en: I am not free and cannot speak loudly.
sentences.ko: 저는 자유롭지 못해서 크게 말할 수 없어요.

sentences.en: If I could speak loudly, I would destroy the cave where Echo lives.
sentences.ko: 크게 말할 수 있다면 메아리가 사는 동굴을 무너뜨릴 거예요.

sentences.en: I would make her thin voice even more hoarse than mine.
sentences.ko: 그녀의 가느다란 목소리를 내 목소리보다 더 쉬게 만들 거예요.

sentences.en: I would do it by making her repeat my Romeo's name over and over.
sentences.ko: 내 로미오라는 이름을 계속 반복하게 만들어서요.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
It is my soul that calls upon my name.
How silver-sweet sound lovers’ tongues by night,
Like softest music to attending ears.

sentences.en: It is my soul that calls my name.
sentences.ko: 제 영혼이 제 이름을 부르고 있어요.

sentences.en: How sweet lovers' voices sound at night.
sentences.ko: 밤에 들리는 연인들의 목소리가 얼마나 달콤한지 몰라요.

sentences.en: They sound like soft music to the ears of those listening.
sentences.ko: 듣는 사람의 귀에는 부드러운 음악처럼 들려요.

speaker: JULIET
raw: Romeo.

sentences.en: Romeo.
sentences.ko: 로미오.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: My dear?

sentences.en: My dear?
sentences.ko: 네, 내 사랑?

speaker: JULIET
raw:
What o’clock tomorrow
Shall I send to thee?

sentences.en: What time tomorrow should I send for you?
sentences.ko: 내일 몇 시에 사람을 보내서 당신을 데려올까요?

speaker: ROMEO
raw: By the hour of nine.

sentences.en: At nine o'clock.
sentences.ko: 아홉 시에요.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
I will not fail. ’Tis twenty years till then.
I have forgot why I did call thee back.

sentences.en: I will not fail.
sentences.ko: 꼭 그렇게 할게요.

sentences.en: It is twenty years until then.
sentences.ko: 그때까지는 20년이나 남았어요.

sentences.en: I have forgotten why I called you back.
sentences.ko: 왜 당신을 다시 불러냈는지 잊어버렸어요.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: Let me stand here till thou remember it.

sentences.en: Let me stand here until you remember it.
sentences.ko: 당신이 기억해낼 때까지 제가 여기 서 있을게요.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
I shall forget, to have thee still stand there,
Remembering how I love thy company.

sentences.en: I will keep forgetting, so that you stay there.
sentences.ko: 당신이 계속 그곳에 머물 수 있도록 저는 계속 잊을게요.

sentences.en: I will only remember how much I love being with you.
sentences.ko: 나는 당신과 함께 있는 게 얼마나 좋은지만 기억할게요.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
And I’ll still stay, to have thee still forget,
Forgetting any other home but this.

sentences.en: And I will stay, so that you keep forgetting.
sentences.ko: 당신이 계속 잊어버릴 수 있게 제가 머무를게요.

sentences.en: I will forget any home but this one.
sentences.ko: 이곳 말고는 다른 집은 다 잊어버릴게요.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
’Tis almost morning; I would have thee gone,
And yet no farther than a wanton’s bird,
That lets it hop a little from her hand,
Like a poor prisoner in his twisted gyves,
And with a silk thread plucks it back again,
So loving-jealous of his liberty.

sentences.en: It is almost morning.
sentences.ko: 거의 아침이에요.

sentences.en: I want you to go.
sentences.ko: 당신이 가셨으면 좋겠어요.

sentences.en: But no farther than a spoiled child's pet bird.
sentences.ko: 하지만 응석받이 아이의 애완 새만큼만 멀리 가세요.

sentences.en: She lets it hop a little from her hand, like a poor prisoner in chains.
sentences.ko: 아이는 사슬에 묶인 불쌍한 죄수 같은 새를 손에서 조금 뛰게 해 줘요.

sentences.en: Then she pulls it back again with a silk thread.
sentences.ko: 그러고는 비단실로 다시 끌어당겨요.

sentences.en: She loves it too much to let it be free.
sentences.ko: 그녀는 새가 자유로워지는 걸 허락하기엔 너무 사랑하거든요.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: I would I were thy bird.

sentences.en: I wish I were your bird.
sentences.ko: 제가 당신의 새였으면 좋겠어요.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Sweet, so would I:
Yet I should kill thee with much cherishing.
Good night, good night. Parting is such sweet sorrow
That I shall say good night till it be morrow.

sentences.en: Sweet, I would too.
sentences.ko: 나도 그러고 싶어요, 내 사랑.

sentences.en: But I would kill you if I held you too closely.
sentences.ko: 하지만 너무 아끼다가 당신을 죽이고 말 거예요.

sentences.en: Good night, good night.
sentences.ko: 안녕히 주무세요, 잘 자요.

sentences.en: Parting is such sweet sorrow.
sentences.ko: 헤어짐은 참 달콤한 슬픔이에요.

sentences.en: I could keep saying good night until morning.
sentences.ko: 아침이 올 때까지 계속 잘 자라고 말하고 싶어요.

raw: Exit.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Sleep dwell upon thine eyes, peace in thy breast.
Would I were sleep and peace, so sweet to rest.
Hence will I to my ghostly Sire’s cell,
His help to crave and my dear hap to tell.

sentences.en: May sleep fall on your eyes and peace be in your breast.
sentences.ko: 잠이 눈에 내리고 가슴에 평화가 깃들길 바라요.

sentences.en: I wish I were sleep and peace to give you such a sweet rest.
sentences.ko: 제가 잠과 평화가 되어 당신에게 달콤한 휴식을 줄 수 있다면 좋겠어요.

sentences.en: I must go now to my priest's small room.
sentences.ko: 이제 신부님의 수도실로 가야 해요.

sentences.en: I will ask for his help and tell him my good fortune.
sentences.ko: 신부님께 도움을 청하고 제 기쁜 소식을 전할게요.

raw: Exit.
